analysis.note: The ending -bhyām is taken as ablative dual with anya, “different from.” The compound is understood as the pair: śruta-prajñā and anumāna-prajñā.

verification.detail: compound stem śrutānumānaprajñā as Stri/Panchami/Dvi: pass; relation dvandva: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Feminine nominative singular, qualifying the supplied sā prajñā in the bhāṣya.

verification.detail: compound stem anyaviṣaya as Stri/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

samasa.vigraha: viśeṣaḥ arthaḥ yasyāḥ sā, tasyā bhāvaḥ

analysis.note: Ablative of cause: “because of being viśeṣārtha.” Here artha is taken as object/content, not purpose; -tva is the abstract-forming suffix in the stem viśeṣārthatva.

verification.detail: compound stem viśeṣārthatva as Napumsaka/Panchami/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

justifications.decision: Translate śrutānumānaprajñābhyām as “from the insights/cognitions of scriptural testimony and inference,” not merely “from what is heard and inferred.”
options_considered: śruta as ordinary “what has been heard”
śruta as āgama-vijñāna, cognition from authoritative testimony
anumāna as a separate prajñā paired with śruta-prajñā
justifications.chosen: śruta means āgama-vijñāna, and anumāna is the parallel inferential cognition; together they form the two prajñās contrasted with samādhi-prajñā.

evidence.translation: Śruta is knowledge from authoritative tradition; it has a general object.
Likewise inference too has a general object.

evidence.quote: tasmāc chrutānumānaprajñābhyām anyaviṣayā sā prajñā viśeṣārthatvād iti.
evidence.translation: Therefore that prajñā has an object different from the prajñās of śruta and inference, because it has the particular as its object.

justifications.decision: Supply “that insight” as the subject and construe anyaviṣayā as feminine singular bahuvrīhi, “having a different object.”
options_considered: anyaviṣayā as an independent plural, “other objects”
anyaviṣayā as feminine singular qualifying an understood prajñā
anyaviṣayā as referring to śruta/anumāna rather than to samādhi-prajñā
justifications.chosen: anyaviṣayā qualifies sā prajñā, the samādhi-born insight, as having an object different from śruta- and anumāna-prajñā.

evidence.quote: tasmāc chrutānumānaprajñābhyām anyaviṣayā sā prajñā viśeṣārthatvād iti.
evidence.translation: Therefore that prajñā has an object different from the prajñās of śruta and inference, because it has the particular as its object.

justifications.decision: Construe it with anya in the sense “different from,” yielding “different from the two cognitions of testimony and inference.”
options_considered: instrumental dual: “different by means of the two cognitions”
ablative dual: “different from the two cognitions”
justifications.chosen: The -bhyām ending in śrutānumānaprajñābhyām is ablative dual.

justifications.decision: Take viśeṣa as the particular not accessible to scripture, inference, or ordinary perception, and artha as object/content rather than purpose.
options_considered: viśeṣārthatvāt as “because of a special purpose”
viśeṣārthatvāt as “because it has particulars as its object”
viśeṣa as a mere species/general class
justifications.chosen: viśeṣārthatvāt means “because its object is the particular.”

evidence.quote: tasmāc chrutānumānaviṣayo na viśeṣaḥ kaścid astīti.
evidence.translation: Therefore no particular at all is an object of śruta and inference.

evidence.quote: na cāsya sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭasya vastuno lokapratyakṣeṇa grahaṇam asti.
evidence.translation: Nor is there grasping of this subtle, hidden, or remote thing by ordinary perception.

evidence.quote: na cāsya viśeṣasyāpramāṇakasyābhāvo 'stīti samādhiprajñānirgrāhya eva sa viśeṣo bhavati bhūtasūkṣmagato vā puruṣagato vā.
evidence.translation: And it is not that this particular, because lacking a means of knowledge, is nonexistent; rather that particular is graspable only by samādhi-prajñā, whether it belongs to subtle elements or to puruṣa.

evidence.quote: tasmāc chrutānumānaprajñābhyām anyaviṣayā sā prajñā viśeṣārthatvād iti.
evidence.translation: Therefore that prajñā has an object different from the prajñās of śruta and inference, because it has the particular as its object.

translation: That insight (prajñā) has an object different from the insights of scriptural testimony (śruta/āgama) and inference (anumāna), because its object is the particular (viśeṣa).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render śruta as simply “what is heard”; Vyāsa specifies śruta as āgamavijñāna, cognition from authoritative tradition, and says it has only a general object.
It might take viśeṣārthatvāt as “because of a special purpose”; the bhāṣya makes viśeṣa the particular grasped by samādhi-prajñā and denied as an object of śruta and anumāna.
It might follow the analyzer’s anyaviṣayāḥ and read “other objects” in the plural; line 9 supplies sā prajñā, confirming feminine singular “that prajñā has a different object.”
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 prints/analyzes anya_viṣayāḥ as viṣaya_PNM, but the unit has anyaviṣayā; the bhāṣya’s sā prajñā (line 9) confirms feminine nominative singular qualifying prajñā, not masculine nominative plural.
ByT5 leaves śrutānumānaprajñābhyām only as a dual feminine form; I resolve -bhyām as ablative dual, not instrumental, because anya in the sense “different from” governs separation.
ByT5 segments viśeṣa_artha_tvāt as though tva were the nominal base separately; I analyze the word as the neuter ablative singular of the abstract stem viśeṣārthatva, with -tva as suffix.
